source.publication: 2025 Montana Individual Income Tax Return Form 2 and Form 2 Instructions
source.section: Form 2 PDF p1 lines 1-8 and PDF p2 worksheet lines 1-13; Instructions PDF p12-13 lines 1-8; PDF p17 tax calculation; PDF p18 rate tables; Instructions PDF p25 Schedule I Line 13; Form 2 PDF p3 line 13; record reliefs working_military_retiree_subtraction and military_survivor_benefit_subtraction

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (person 0) 30,000.00 + military pension (person 0) 40,000.00 = 70,000.00. Federal taxable income = 70,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 = 54,250.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). Filing status single, no Montana standard deduction or exemptions. Schedule I Part I: line 7 additions 0.00; line 24 subtractions 0.00. Form 2 page 1: line 1 federal AGI 70,000.00; line 2 Form 1040 lines 12e and 13b 15,750.00; line 3 54,250.00; line 4 0.00; line 5 0.00; line 6 age 65 subtraction 0 x 5,660.00 = 0.00; line 7 Montana taxable income 54,250.00 + 0.00 - 0.00 - 0.00 = 54,250.00. Page 2 worksheet: line 1 taxable income 54,250.00; no net long-term capital gain, so lines 2-10 are skipped and line 11 is 0.00; line 12 ordinary income tax from the PDF p18 rate table: 5.9% x 54,250.00 = 3,200.75, less 253 = 2,947.75; line 13 = 2,947.75, carried to page 1 line 8. Bracket schedule as numbers (the expected figure): 4.7% x 21,100.00 = 991.70; 5.9% x (54,250.00 - 21,100.00 = 33,150.00) = 1,955.85; bracket tax 2,947.55. Line 9 nonrefundable credits 0.00; line 10 tax after credits 2,947.55. The form gives 2,947.75; expected keeps the projection's 2,947.55, a difference of 0.20 from the table's whole-dollar constant (253 against 253.20). The booklet would go further: Schedule I line 13 for an eligible working retiree: the lesser of 50% x 40,000.00 = 20,000.00 and Montana earned income 30,000.00 = 20,000.00, assuming every residency test is met, so line 7 would be 34,250.00 and the tax 1,767.75 by the rate table. Expected follows the projection, which keeps it in income. The projection leaves the subtraction out (not_modelled, warning has_military_pension): the earned income limit and the five-year limit cannot be represented.
accepted_approximations: The working military retiree and survivor subtractions are left out, because their earned income limit and five-year limit cannot be represented and an uncapped 50% would wrongly reach retirees with no Montana earned income, every year for life.
The tables print a whole-dollar constant with the 5.9% rate (253, 506, 380) where the bracket arithmetic gives 253.20, 506.40, 380.40.
